assessment_summary: The statement is false. While the closure of an intersection is always a subset of the intersection of the closures, the reverse inclusion does not hold in general. A simple counterexample using open intervals in the real numbers demonstrates this.
counterexample: Let the ambient space X be the real numbers with the standard topology. Let A = (0, 1) and B = (1, 2). Their intersection A intersect B is the empty set, so cl(A intersect B) = cl(empty set) = empty set. However, their closures are cl(A) = [0, 1] and cl(B) = [1, 2], and their intersection cl(A) intersect cl(B) = {1}. Since the empty set does not equal {1}, the statement cl(A intersect B) = cl(A) intersect cl(B) is false.
